id.s1.criterion:
- Damaged area and surrounding skin are clean and bare enough that individual rivet heads are distinguishable
- No dirt, grease or loose paint obscures the damage or the fasteners around it
- The full damage feature (crack, hole, dent) is exposed and unobstructed in the frame

sources.condition: Dirt, grease and paint are removed from the damaged area and surrounding structure so each rivet and fastener is visible.
sources.note: Handbook: "Remove all dirt, grease, and paint from the damaged and surrounding areas to determine the exact condition of each rivet, bolt, and weld."

sources.condition: Inspection extends into the adjacent area, covering skin wrinkles, dents, loose rivets and abrasions, not just the obvious damage.
sources.note: Handbook: "Inspect skin for wrinkles throughout a large area" and "Check all skin, dents, and wrinkles for any cracks or abrasions."

sources.condition: Any movable parts in the inspected area are operated and confirmed to function normally.
sources.note: Handbook: "Check the operation of all movable parts in the area."

sources.condition: Damage type is named and classified, with a stated determination that repair rather than replacement is appropriate.
sources.note: Handbook: "Determine if repair would be the best procedure"; damage classes given on p.4-90.

not_photo_gradeable: How far beyond the damage the inspection actually swept
Whether movable parts in the area were operated and checked
Whether the damage was correctly classified and a repair-vs-replace decision made
id.s1.required_framing: One overall shot of the cleaned damage area including several inches of surrounding structure and the nearest rivet rows, taken square to the surface with the damage centered and lit to show surface texture.

id.s2.step_text: Measure the extent of the damage.
id.s2.criterion:
- A steel scale lies flat on the workpiece, spanning the damage's greatest dimension
- The scale's zero end is set at the edge of the damage, not offset
- The damaged area and its surroundings are clean and free of grease or flaking paint
- The full damage boundary, including crack ends, is visible within the frame alongside the scale

sources.condition: Recorded height and length capture the full extent of the damage, including crack tips and adjacent affected area.
sources.note: Handbook: "the extent of damage must be fully evaluated" and "Check all skin, dents, and wrinkles for any cracks or abrasions."

sources.condition: A steel scale rests flat on the surface, spanning the damage's greatest dimension with its zero at the damage edge.
sources.note: Senior Mechanic Note 1: "Use a steel scale to find the damage's height and length."

sources.condition: The damaged and surrounding area is free of dirt, grease and loose paint so the damage boundary is unambiguous.
sources.note: "Remove all dirt, grease, and paint from the damaged and surrounding areas to determine the exact condition".

sources.condition: Measured dimensions are compared against the permissible damage limits for that component before a repair class is chosen.
sources.note: "Permissible limits for negligible damage vary for different components of different aircraft and should be carefully researched on an individual basis."

not_photo_gradeable: The actual numeric height and length values of the damage
Whether the measurement captured the full extent, including subsurface or hidden crack propagation
Comparison of measured dimensions to permissible negligible-damage limits in the applicable manual
id.s2.required_framing: Shoot perpendicular to the panel, close enough that the scale graduations are legible, with the entire damage outline and both ends of the scale inside the frame.

id.s3.step_text: Mark the repair area with a marker around all of the damage.
id.s3.criterion:
- A continuous marker line completely encloses the damaged area with no damage extending past it
- Outline is circular, oval, or has visibly rounded corners; no square corners
- Line is drawn in marker on undamaged skin, not scribed or scratched into the metal
- The damage itself remains visible inside the marked boundary

sources.condition: The marker outline fully encircles the damage, with every crack tip, dent edge and abrasion inside the line.
sources.note: Procedure sheet: mark "around all of the damage"; handbook 4-92 "Remove all distorted skin and structure in damaged area."

sources.condition: The outline is circular or oval, or if rectangular has visibly rounded rather than square corners.
sources.note: Handbook: "try to make cutouts either circular or oval in shape"; also p.4-92 "Round all square corners."

sources.condition: Rectangular marked corners carry a radius of no less than 1/2 inch.
sources.note: Handbook: "make the radius of curvature at each corner no smaller than 1/2-inch" for rectangular cutouts.

sources.condition: The marked boundary lies outside the measured damage extent by a clear margin on all sides, in sound metal.
sources.note: Compare outline to the height/length taken with the steel scale; handbook 4-92: edges of completed repair match existing structure.

not_photo_gradeable: Corner radius of a rectangular outline meeting the 1/2-inch minimum
Actual clearance between the marked line and the measured extent of the damage
Agreement of the marked dimensions with the scale measurements taken in the previous step
id.s3.required_framing: Shoot square-on (perpendicular) to the panel from directly above the marked area, close enough that the whole marker outline and surrounding undamaged skin are in frame, with a steel scale laid beside the outline for dimension reference and even lighting so the marker line and the damage inside it are both legible.
conflicts: Procedure sheet (Create the Patch Doubler, note 3) calls for 1/8" corner radii on cut shapes, while the handbook p.4-86 requires rectangular cutout corner radii no smaller than 1/2-inch and p.4-96 requires patch corners rounded to no less than 1/4-inch; the procedure sheet is operative as taught.

rd.s1.step_text: Cut out or stop the damage from spreading.
rd.s1.criterion:
- No visible crack, tear or buckled metal remains inside the cut perimeter
- A stop hole is present at each end of every crack, with the crack tip ending inside the hole
- Opening is circular/oval or all corners are visibly rounded, no square corners
- Skin surrounding the opening shows no saw skips, gouges or cuts past the marked line

sources.condition: No crack, tear or distorted material remains inside the cut perimeter; the damage is fully excised or arrested.
sources.note: Handbook p.4-92 damage removal: "Remove all distorted skin and structure in damaged area"; procedure sheet step 1.

sources.condition: A stop hole 3/32-inch diameter is drilled at each crack end so the hole encloses the crack tip.
sources.note: Handbook p.4-96 figure: "Stop holes—drill 3/32" diameter holes in each sharp corner"; p.4-93 "a small hole must be drilled in each end".

sources.condition: The cutout is circular/oval or has rounded corners — no square corners remain in the opening.
sources.note: "Round all square corners"; p.4-86 "try to make cutouts either circular or oval in shape", rectangular corner radius "no smaller than 1/2-inch" (measured separately).

sources.condition: Surrounding skin outside the marked repair area is free of saw skips, gouges or overcuts.
sources.note: Handbook p.4-92: "Remove damaged material so that the edges of the completed repair match existing structure and aircraft lines."

not_photo_gradeable: 3/32-inch stop hole diameter
Minimum 1/2-inch corner radius for a rectangular cutout
Confirmation that a hairline crack tip is fully captured (may need magnification or NDI)
rd.s1.required_framing: Close-up perpendicular to the skin showing the whole cut opening and both crack ends with stop holes, with a steel scale laid alongside the opening for size reference.

rd.s2.step_text: Smooth and deburr all cut edges.
rd.s2.criterion:
- All cut edges show no burrs, slivers or nicks along their full length
- Cutout corners are visibly rounded, none left square
- No coarse scratch pattern or file marks remain on the edge or adjacent skin
- Cut perimeter still lies on/inside the marker layout line, not gouged past it

sources.condition: All cut edges are free of burrs, feathered slivers, nicks and visible tool/scratch marks.
sources.note: Handbook p.4-92: "Smooth out any abrasions and/or dents"; procedure sheet note requires removing sharp edges and scratches.

sources.condition: Every corner of the cutout is rounded, with no square or sharp corner remaining.
sources.note: Damage Removal list: "Round all square corners"; also figure 4-176 "cut to a smooth rectangle with corner radii".

sources.condition: Corner radius of a rectangular cutout measures no smaller than 1/2 inch.
sources.note: "make the radius of curvature at each corner no smaller than 1⁄2-inch"; procedure sheet gives no cutout radius figure.

sources.condition: Sanding progressed from coarse grit through to fine grit rather than a single grit.
sources.note: Senior Mechanic Note 2: start coarse-grit progressing to fine-grit; handbook is qualitative only.

not_photo_gradeable: Corner radius of the cutout is at least 1/2 inch (needs a radius gauge or scale reading)
Grit progression from coarse to fine during sanding (only visible while the action is performed)
rd.s2.required_framing: Close-up shot square to the skin showing the entire cutout perimeter with the marker layout line visible, plus one low-angle/raking-light shot along the cut edges so burrs and scratches read.
conflicts: Procedure sheet specifies a 1/8" corner radius (on the doubler) while the handbook p.4-86 requires rectangular cutout corner radii no smaller than 1/2"; procedure sheet is operative as taught, but the cutout radius standard needs instructor confirmation.

cp.s1.criterion:
- A single continuous traced outline appears on the blank, matching the opening perimeter including corner radii
- Material remains outside the traced line on all sides of the blank
- Only one trace attempt is visible; no smeared, doubled or abandoned lines
- The traced line is thin and crisp, consistent with a fine-tip marker

sources.condition: The traced outline on the blank reproduces the opening's full perimeter as one continuous fine line, with no gaps, double lines or corner deviation.
sources.note: Procedure sheet: "Use a fine-tip marker to trace the shape accurately."

sources.condition: The blank extends past the traced line on every side, leaving margin material outside the line for cutting and filing.
sources.note: Procedure sheet: "a piece of sheet metal larger than the opening"; margin needed for later cut-outside-the-line step.

sources.condition: The blank chosen for the filler is the same gauge and alloy as the original skin.
sources.note: Handbook: "The filler must be of the same gauge and material as the original skin." Gauge verified by micrometer, alloy by stock marking.

sources.condition: The blank is held flat and flush against the underside of the skin throughout tracing, without tilt or lift.
sources.note: Procedure sheet: "against the underside, pressing it flush"; only observable while the trace is made.

not_photo_gradeable: Filler blank is the same gauge as the original skin (micrometer reading)
Filler blank is the same alloy as the original skin (stock marking/spec)
Blank was pressed flush against the underside of the skin while tracing
cp.s1.required_framing: One overhead, square-on shot of the marked blank with its whole traced outline and all four edges in frame, taken next to the skin opening so the shapes can be compared.

cp.s2.step_text: Remove and cut out the shape.
cp.s2.criterion:
- Cut edge is outside the traced outline on all sides and the marker line is still visible on the blank
- No cut, nick or notch crosses inside the traced outline
- Cut edges show no tears, cracks, curling or buckling from the cutting tool
- Blank is a single piece matching the traced shape, corners not cut square into the outline

sources.condition: The cut edge lies entirely outside the traced outline, with the marker line still visible on the blank.
sources.note: Senior Mechanic Note: cut close to the marked line, leaving a small amount of material outside the line.

sources.condition: Excess material left outside the traced line is small and reasonably uniform, filable to fit without reworking the whole edge.
sources.note: 'Small amount of material outside the line' is qualitative; the actual margin must be measured off the blank.

sources.condition: Cut edges are free of tears, cracks, curl or buckling, and no nick crosses inside the outline.
sources.note: Handbook p.4-93: damage 'must be cleaned and smoothed'; p.4-92 'Smooth out any abrasions and/or dents.'

sources.condition: The blank was cut from stock of the same gauge and alloy as the original skin.
sources.note: Handbook: 'The filler must be of the same gauge and material as the original skin.' Verified by micrometer/stock marking, not by sight.

not_photo_gradeable: Actual dimension of the excess margin left outside the line
Gauge (thickness) of the filler stock versus the original skin
Alloy/material identity of the filler stock
Whether the blank will file down to a flush fit in the opening
cp.s2.required_framing: Lay the cut blank flat, traced-line side up, with a steel scale in frame alongside the cut edge; include a second shot of the blank held over the skin opening so the outline and cut edge are both visible.

cp.s3.step_text: Size material to fit the shape.
cp.s3.criterion:
- Filler is seated in the opening and flush with the surrounding skin, no step or bulge
- Gap around the full perimeter is uniform, with no wedge-shaped or oversized gap
- Filed edges are straight and square, with no gouges, waviness, or burrs
- No hammer marks, upset skin, or distortion around the opening edge

sources.condition: The filler seats fully in the opening and sits flush with the surrounding skin, with no step, lip, or bulge.
sources.note: Handbook: "A flush patch is a filler patch that is flush to the skin when applied"; p.4-93 requires "a smooth outside surface".

sources.condition: The gap between filler and opening edge is uniform around the full perimeter, with no wedge-shaped or crescent gap.
sources.note: Procedure sheet: file "until the patch fits the opening"; handbook speaks only qualitatively of fit and contour.

sources.condition: Filed edges are straight and square to the surface, free of file gouges, waviness, and burrs.
sources.note: Procedure sheet step 4 deburr/smooth; handbook p.4-92 "Smooth out any abrasions and/or dents" and "Round all square corners".

sources.condition: The filler material is the same gauge and alloy as the original skin after fitting.
sources.note: Handbook: "The filler must be of the same gauge and material as the original skin." Verify with micrometer/material marking.

sources.condition: The filler enters the opening by hand without forcing, hammering, or rocking in place.
sources.note: Senior Mechanic Note: file "carefully remove material until the patch fits the opening" — fit judged during trial fitting.

not_photo_gradeable: Filler gauge and alloy match the original skin (micrometer/material marking)
Filler enters the opening by hand without forcing or rocking (trial fit must be watched)
cp.s3.required_framing: One shot straight down (lens perpendicular) on the filler seated in the opening with the entire perimeter in frame, plus one low-angle raking shot across the joint line to show flushness; include a scale beside the opening.

cp.s4.step_text: Deburr edges and smooth scratches with sandpaper.
cp.s4.criterion:
- Filler edges show no burrs, slivers or ragged sections along their full perimeter
- Edge finish is uniform all the way around, with no localized flats or gouges from filing
- No coarse file or coarse-grit scratch marks visible on either face or on the edges
- Corners are smooth and free of sharp points

sources.condition: All cut edges and hole edges of the filler are burr-free and uniformly smooth, with no sharp or ragged sections.
sources.note: Procedure sheet step 4 and safety note 1 (cut/formed metal leaves sharp edges); handbook defines burr as 'a small, thin section of metal extending beyond a regular surface'.

sources.condition: No coarse file marks or deep scratches remain on the filler faces or edges after final sanding.
sources.note: Handbook p.4-89: 'Scratches, which penetrate the pure aluminum surface layer, permit corrosion to take place in the alloy beneath.'

sources.condition: After sanding, the filler still fits the opening with a uniform gap and no oversize slop from removed material.
sources.note: Procedure sheet Create the Patch Filler note 3: file 'until the patch fits the opening'; fit gap must be gauged, not eyeballed.

sources.condition: Filler thickness is unchanged by face sanding and still matches the original skin gauge.
sources.note: Handbook: 'The filler must be of the same gauge and material as the original skin.' Requires micrometer reading.

not_photo_gradeable: Filler thickness still equal to the original skin gauge after sanding
Actual filler-to-opening gap dimension / snugness of fit
Grit progression from coarse to fine actually used during sanding
cp.s4.required_framing: Filler removed from the opening and laid on a clean bench, photographed close-up under raking light so one full face and the entire cut edge are visible; include a scale alongside and a second frame of the reverse face.

pr.s1.step_text: Choose the rivet for the repair.
pr.s1.criterion:
- The selected rivet head style matches the head style of the existing rivets in the surrounding skin
- All rivets set aside for the repair are one consistent diameter and length, with no mixed sizes

sources.condition: Selected rivet diameter equals the next standard size above three times the measured skin thickness.
sources.note: Handbook: "multiply the thickness of the skin by three and use the next larger size rivet corresponding to that figure"; procedure sheet only says "calculate".

sources.condition: Rivet type and material match the original rivets in the part being repaired.
sources.note: Handbook: "the rivet size and material should be the same as the original rivets in the part being repaired."

sources.condition: Rivet length provides grip for the full doubler-plus-skin-plus-filler stack with enough shank left to upset a shop head.
sources.note: Procedure sheet note: "Calculate the required rivet diameter and length." No numeric length rule appears in the handbook extract.

sources.condition: Selected rivet head style (universal or countersunk) matches the existing rivet heads in the surrounding skin.
sources.note: Rests on handbook "the rivet size and material should be the same as the original rivets"; head style comparison is visually settleable.

not_photo_gradeable: Rivet diameter equals next size above 3 × measured skin thickness
Rivet length sufficient for total stack grip plus shop head material
Rivet material/type identical to original rivets in the part
pr.s1.required_framing: Lay the chosen rivet on the work beside a scale or caliper showing its diameter and length, with the written diameter/length calculation and the existing skin rivets in the same frame.

pr.s2.step_text: Determine and plot the edge distance.
pr.s2.criterion:
- Edge distance lines are visible on all edges of the doubler, filler, and skin repair area
- Each line is parallel to its edge and at a visibly constant offset
- Corner intersections of the edge distance lines are clean and complete
- Lines are drawn fine and legible, not smeared or doubled

sources.condition: Edge distance lines are marked on all four edges of the doubler, the filler, and the skin repair area.
sources.note: Senior Mechanic Note: "Mark that distance from all edges with a marker"; handbook is qualitative on layout.

sources.condition: Each marked edge distance measures the value calculated for the selected rivet diameter, and no less.
sources.note: Handbook: "the proper edge distance for the larger rivet must be maintained"; the numeric value comes from the student's calculation.

sources.condition: Marked edge distance meets the handbook minimum for the rivet size used, e.g. 1/4" for 1/8" rivets.
sources.note: Figure 4-175 text: "Minimum edge distance using 1/8" rivets is 1/4" and using 5/32" rivets is 5/16"" (stated for lap/scab patch).

sources.condition: Each line runs parallel to its edge at a constant offset, and lines meet cleanly at the corners.
sources.note: Layout must be usable for pitch plotting; handbook only requires patterns "conform to instructions in the applicable aircraft manual".

sources.condition: Rivet diameter used in the edge distance calculation matches the rivet chosen in step 1 of the layout.
sources.note: Perform Rivet Layout notes 1-2 require the calculated diameter to drive the edge distance figure.

not_photo_gradeable: Actual measured edge distance versus the calculated value
Conformance to the handbook minimum (1/4" for 1/8" rivets, 5/16" for 5/32" rivets)
Whether the calculation was based on the rivet diameter selected in the prior step
pr.s2.required_framing: Lay the doubler, filler, and marked skin flat, shot square from above with a 6" steel scale placed alongside one marked edge so the offset and the ruler graduations are both readable.

pr.s3.step_text: Determine the pitch and plot each rivet.
pr.s3.criterion:
- Dots are plotted along the full length of every rivet row, none omitted
- Each dot lies on the previously marked edge-distance line
- Rows are symmetrical about the opening and dots appear evenly spaced
- Dots are single, small and crisp with no smears or duplicate marks
- Layout marks appear on each mating piece shown in the frame

sources.condition: Adjacent dots along each rivet line are spaced at the calculated pitch, equal to one another within layout tolerance.
sources.note: Sheet: "Calculate the needed pitch. Mark a dot at that interval on each material"; requires scale reading between dots.

sources.condition: The plotted pitch and rivet count match the documented calculation and the applicable manual's rivet pattern.
sources.note: Handbook p.4-92: "The rivet pattern for a repair must conform to instructions in the applicable aircraft manual"; count from Figure 4-169.

sources.condition: Every dot sits on the previously plotted edge-distance lines, with rows symmetrical about the opening and none outside the layout.
sources.note: Sheet step 2 plots edge distance first; dots must fall on those lines for a valid pattern.

sources.condition: On a lap or scab patch layout, rows are staggered about 1/2 inch apart with spacing about 1 inch.
sources.note: Handbook: "Space rivets aproximately 1" apart in staggered rows 1/2" apart"; applies to lap/scab patch geometry only.

not_photo_gradeable: Actual pitch dimension between adjacent dots and its evenness
Whether the plotted rivet count matches the calculated/manual-required number
Approximately 1 inch spacing and 1/2 inch stagger for a lap patch
Correctness of the underlying pitch calculation
pr.s3.required_framing: Shoot square-on (perpendicular) to the marked surface so the whole layout and its edges are in frame, with a steel scale laid alongside one rivet row and all marked pieces visible.

dh.s1.step_text: Center punch the holes in the skin.
dh.s1.criterion:
- One punch indentation is present at every plotted rivet mark on the skin
- Each indentation sits centered on its layout mark, not beside or straddling it
- Indentations are round and cleanly formed, not elongated or smeared from a canted punch
- No stray, doubled or extra indentations appear outside the rivet layout

sources.condition: Every plotted rivet mark on the skin carries exactly one punch indentation centered on the mark, with no stray or doubled indentations.
sources.note: Senior Mechanic Notes: "Place the point of the center punch directly on a mark for a rivet" and "Repeat for all rivet mark locations on the skin."

sources.condition: Measured punch-center locations match the plotted edge distance and pitch for the repair layout.
sources.note: Handbook: "The rivet pattern for a repair must conform to instructions in the applicable aircraft manual"; procedure sheet plots ED and pitch marks.

sources.condition: The skin around each indentation remains flat, with no warping, dishing or backside bulge from an over-heavy blow.
sources.note: Senior Mechanic Note: "One light blow is enough; too heavy and the metal will warp"; verify with straightedge/flatness check.

sources.condition: The punch is held perpendicular and steady against the skin and struck with a single light hammer blow.
sources.note: Senior Mechanic Notes: "Hold the punch steady against the material" and "Lightly tap the top of the center punch".

not_photo_gradeable: Measured edge distance and pitch of the punch centers against the plotted layout
Flatness of the skin / absence of warping or backside bulge from the punch blow
Punch held perpendicular and steady with a single light hammer blow
dh.s1.required_framing: Shoot square-on (perpendicular) close-up of the marked repair area on the skin, with raking light so the indentations read, all layout lines and every punch mark inside frame, and a 6" scale laid alongside the rivet row.

dh.s2.step_text: Drill pilot holes through the marks.
dh.s2.criterion:
- Every pilot hole sits centered on its center-punch mark with layout marks still visible
- Holes are round, not oval, elongated or torn at the edges
- Hole pattern follows the marked edge-distance and pitch lines with no hole crowding an edge
- Skin surface around the holes is free of gouges, chuck marks or breakout petals

sources.condition: Each pilot hole is centered on its center-punch mark, with layout dots still visible around the hole rim.
sources.note: Sheet directs the bit apex be positioned in the punch indentation and holes drilled through the marks, preserving edge distance and pitch.

sources.condition: Pilot holes are round and clean, with no elongation, ovalling, tearing or crescent gouging at the hole edge.
sources.note: Handbook: "Drill bits that do not cut satisfactorily cause damage to the hole."

sources.condition: Pilot bit diameter is no larger than the rivet diameter, #40 (0.098") for a 1/8" rivet.
sources.note: Sheet: bit "same size as or slightly smaller than the rivet diameter... #40 drill bits are preferred"; handbook gives no such figure.

sources.condition: Drill is held perpendicular with the part clamped or backed while drilling, and exit is controlled at breakout.
sources.note: Sheet: keep drill perpendicular, anticipate exit; handbook mentions clamping and a wood support only in the titanium hand-drilling context.

not_photo_gradeable: Pilot bit diameter (#40 / no larger than rivet diameter) — requires bit or hole measurement
Drill held perpendicular to the material through the cut — only visible while drilling
Part clamped or supported behind while drilling
Controlled anticipation of bit exit at the back face
dh.s2.required_framing: Single shot square-on (lens perpendicular) to the drilled surface, whole hole pattern in frame with the layout lines and a scale alongside; include a second angled shot of the back face if breakout is a concern.

dh.s3.criterion:
- Cleco pins installed through the transferred holes with the doubler flat against the skin
- Doubler holes concentric with skin holes; no crescent-shaped, doubled or torn openings
- Cleco clamps or pins present at the perimeter of the drilled area in the finished work
- Doubler edges intact, no hole broken out to an edge or corner

sources.condition: Every drilled doubler hole is concentric with its mating skin hole, with cleco pins seated fully and no crescent or double-drilled openings.
sources.note: Sheet: 'Transfer holes from the skin to the doubler... Drill a hole and hold it aligned with a cleco pin.'

sources.condition: The doubler is held with cleco clamps or pins so it cannot shift between the first and last hole drilled.
sources.note: Sheet: 'Secure in place with cleco clamps, if possible'; only observable while drilling progresses.

sources.condition: Hole centers on the doubler sit at the laid-out edge distance from the doubler edges, with the ED line bisecting the transferred skin holes.
sources.note: Sheet: 'Bisect the holes in the skin with the edge distance line on the doubler.' Handbook only states edge distance 'must be maintained' qualitatively.

sources.condition: Pilot holes are drilled with a bit no larger than the rivet diameter (#40 preferred for a 1/8" rivet).
sources.note: Sheet note 6: bit 'same size as or slightly smaller than the rivet diameter... #40 drill bits are preferred'; figure is the sheet's alone.

not_photo_gradeable: Edge distance dimension from hole center to doubler edge
Pilot hole diameter / drill bit size used
Whether the doubler was clamped and stayed aligned throughout drilling
Drill perpendicularity during the cut
dh.s3.required_framing: Shoot the skin side square-on with the doubler clecoed in place, close enough that individual holes, cleco pins and the doubler's edge margins are all visible in one frame.

dh.s4.criterion:
- Each filler hole is round and full-size, with no teardrop, oval or crescent from a wandering bit
- Filler seats in the opening flush with the surrounding skin, no lip, gap or overlap
- Cleco pins pass through filler and doubler holes and seat without forcing
- Filler is flat: no warp, dish or bulge around punch marks and holes

sources.condition: Every hole in the filler is round and full-size, with no teardrop, elongation or double-drilled crescent.
sources.note: Handbook warns of "holes that have been elongated" and "if the rivet holes show elongation, replace the rivets with the next larger size" (p.4-91/4-92).

sources.condition: Filler holes hold the laid-out edge distance and pitch from every filler edge.
sources.note: Procedure sheet requires plotted ED and pitch; handbook only states "The rivet pattern for a repair must conform to instructions in the applicable aircraft manual" (p.4-92).

sources.condition: Filler sits in the opening flush with the skin and its holes register with the doubler on cleco pins.
sources.note: Procedure sheet: fit into opening and transfer holes to doubler; handbook: "A flush patch is a filler patch that is flush to the skin" (p.4-96).

sources.condition: Filler shows no warp, dishing or bulge around the punched and drilled holes.
sources.note: Senior Mechanic Note: "One light blow is enough; too heavy and the metal will warp"; handbook lists upsetting as a defect (p.4-90).

sources.condition: Drill is held perpendicular with the filler clamped or backed while drilling.
sources.note: Procedure sheet note 12; handbook: "When hand drilling thin or flexible parts, put a support (such as a block of wood) behind the part" (p.4-85).

not_photo_gradeable: Edge distance and pitch dimensions of the filler holes
Finished hole diameter relative to rivet diameter
Drill held perpendicular with the part clamped or backed during drilling
Light single center-punch blow technique
dh.s4.required_framing: One close, square-on shot of the filler seated in the opening with cleco pins installed, plus one close-up of the filler's hole line with a steel scale laid alongside so edge distance and pitch can be read.

dh.s5.step_text: Step up to the next drill bit size.
dh.s5.criterion:
- Every layout hole is enlarged to a single uniform finished size, none left at pilot size
- Holes are round with no tearing, lobing or elongation at the edges
- Cleco pins or clamps remain installed through the stack during and after enlargement
- Skin, doubler and filler holes are concentric with no visible offset between layers
- Drill bit is chucked with the full flute length exposed clear of the jaws

sources.condition: The final hole diameter is at least 0.003 in larger than the rivet diameter (e.g. #30, 0.1285 in, for a -4 rivet).
sources.note: Senior Mechanic Note 17 gives the ream dimension; handbook pages speak only qualitatively about hole size and rivet fit.

sources.condition: The step-up sequence is pilot #40 then finish size, with no size skipped past the specified increment.
sources.note: Notes 6 and 17 fix pilot (#40) and finish (#30) bits; handbook increments (0.0313/0.0625 in) apply only to titanium holes 0.1875 in and larger.

sources.condition: Finished holes are round and clean, with no elongation, tearing or triangular lobing at the hole edge.
sources.note: "Drill bits that do not cut satisfactorily cause damage to the hole"; p.4-91 warns of "holes that have been elongated."

sources.condition: Skin, doubler and filler remain clamped or clecoed together while holes are enlarged, so the stack stays aligned.
sources.note: Handbook: "clamp them together tightly... use temporary bolts, Cleco clamps" (stated for titanium hand drilling); procedure notes 14-16 require cleco pins.

sources.condition: The new bit is chucked with the flutes fully exposed clear of the chuck jaws.
sources.note: Senior Mechanic Note 7: "Install drill bit into pneumatic drill with flutes fully exposed."

not_photo_gradeable: Final hole diameter being at least 0.003 in larger than the rivet diameter
Identification of the actual pilot and finish bit sizes used (#40, #30)
Chuck tightened with the chuck key
Drill held perpendicular with moderate pressure during enlargement
dh.s5.required_framing: Square-on close-up of the clecoed patch assembly filling the frame so all enlarged holes and the cleco pins are visible; include a second frame of the drill with the finish bit chucked next to a drill gauge or scale.

dh.s6.step_text: Drill all holes up to the finished size.
dh.s6.criterion:
- Every layout hole in skin, doubler and filler is drilled through at one uniform finished size
- Holes are round with clean, unturn bore edges — no elongation, crescents or tear-out
- Holes line up through all layers with no visible step or offset between sheets
- No stray or duplicate holes outside the plotted rivet pattern

sources.condition: Each finished hole measures at least 0.003" larger than the rivet diameter (e.g., 0.1285"/#30 for a -4 rivet).
sources.note: Procedure sheet Senior Mechanic Note 17 gives the ream dimension; handbook pages supplied state no such figure.

sources.condition: Finished holes are round and clean-edged, with no elongation, tri-lobing or torn bore walls.
sources.note: "Drill bits that do not cut satisfactorily cause damage to the hole"; p.4-91 treats elongated holes as defects.

sources.condition: Holes remain concentric through skin, doubler and filler with no step or crescent between layers.
sources.note: Handbook treats "holes in the sheet misaligned" as a defect condition; procedure sheet requires cleco pinning to hold alignment.

sources.condition: Edge distance to the plotted layout lines is still met after enlarging holes to finished size.
sources.note: "the proper edge distance for the larger rivet must be maintained" when a hole is enlarged.

not_photo_gradeable: Finished hole diameter being at least 0.003" over rivet diameter (needs pin gauge or drill/bit reading)
Edge distance measurement after enlargement
Drill held perpendicular with moderate pressure during drilling
Clecos kept installed in adjacent holes while remaining holes were drilled
dh.s6.required_framing: Perpendicular close-up of the assembled repair, lit so all finished holes are in frame; take one shot with clecos in place and one with the pattern clear so hole roundness and layer alignment are visible.

dh.s7.step_text: Deburr all drilled holes from both sides.
dh.s7.criterion:
- Every drilled hole edge is clean and smooth, with no raised metal ring or curl of swarf on either visible face
- Skin, doubler and filler are shown separated so both faces of the drilled holes are in view
- Faying surfaces and hole edges are clear of chips, shavings and marker debris
- Hole edges show only a light break, not a visible countersink or feathered knife edge
- Surrounding skin shows no gouges or spiral scratches from the deburr tool

sources.condition: No raised metal or burr ring remains around any drilled hole on either face of skin, doubler and filler.

sources.condition: Hole diameter after deburring is still at the finished/ream size and not enlarged or knife-edged by the deburr tool.
sources.note: Sheet: ream "at least 0.003" larger than the rivet diameter" (e.g., #30 = 0.1285" for a -4 rivet); handbook gives no deburr dimension.

sources.condition: Parts were separated so the faying (hidden) faces of every hole were deburred, not just the exposed sides.
sources.note: "from both sides" — the blind face cannot be verified once the assembly is re-clecoed.

sources.condition: Faying surfaces and hole edges are free of chips, shavings and FOD before reassembly.
sources.note: Sheet equipment list includes FOD box; trapped swarf prevents parts sitting flush.

not_photo_gradeable: Hole diameter/ream size remaining within 0.003" over rivet diameter after deburring
That the blind/faying face of each hole was actually deburred rather than assembled untouched
Absence of burrs on faces already reassembled and clecoed together
dh.s7.required_framing: Lay the skin, doubler and filler side by side, unclecoed, with the drilled faces up under raking light; take one close-up perpendicular to the surface covering the full hole pattern, then flip all parts and repeat so both faces of every hole are shown, with a scale in frame.

sr.s1.criterion:

- Retaining spring form matches the set: cone-shaped with a universal set, cylindrical with a countersunk set

sources.condition: The selected set's tip style matches the rivet head style to be driven — concave recess for universal, flat disk for countersunk.
sources.note: Sheet: universal set has 'concave recess on tip'; countersunk set has 'disk-shaped head'. Handbook extract does not cover rivet gun sets.

sources.condition: The concave recess diameter equals the rivet head diameter, neither undersized nor oversized.

sources.condition: The retaining spring form matches the chosen set — cone-shaped for a universal set, cylindrical for a countersunk set.

not_photo_gradeable: Concave recess diameter equals the rivet head diameter (requires measuring or gauging against the actual rivet)
Correct thread fit of set/spring to the specific rivet gun

not_photo_gradeable: Spring tightened until a high rise in torque is felt
Set is captive and will not eject when the gun is fired or inverted

sources.condition: Shop head is round and concentric on the shank, not clinched, tipped or joggled to one side.

Backing support used while punching

- The vacated hole appears circular, with no elongation, oval shape or crescent bite on one side

task.criterion:
- The marked repair boundary encloses every crack tip, dent edge and abrasion, and lies in sound metal outside the measured damage extent on all sides.
- The cutout has no square corners; a rectangular cutout carries a corner radius no smaller than 1/2 inch, and cracks that are stop-drilled use 3/32-inch holes at each crack end.
- All cut edges of skin, doubler and filler are burr-free and smoothed, with no feathered slivers, nicks or coarse tool marks remaining.
- The filler is the same gauge and material as the original skin; the doubler is one gauge heavier than the skin.
- Rivet diameter is the next larger standard size above three times the skin thickness, and rivet type, material and head style match the existing rivets in the part.
- Edge-distance lines are marked on every edge of doubler, filler and skin repair area at a constant offset, and the marked distance is not less than the minimum for the rivet size used (1/4 inch for 1/8-inch rivets, 5/16 inch for 5/32-inch rivets).
- Plotted rivet dots sit on the edge-distance lines at a uniform pitch, symmetrical about the opening, and match the documented rivet-count calculation.
- Every finished hole is round, concentric through skin, doubler and filler, and at least 0.003 inch larger than the rivet diameter; all holes are deburred on both faces.
- The filler seats flush with the surrounding skin with a uniform perimeter gap, no step, lip, bulge or wedge-shaped gap.
- All manufactured heads are flush and seated with no gap or tipping; surrounding skin is free of bucking-bar dents, set 'smileys' and dishing.
- Each shop head measures approximately 0.5 x shank diameter in height and 1.5 x shank diameter in width, is concentric with the shank, and is not clinched, cocked or joggled.
- Any rivet head cracking is within limits: depth less than 1/8 of the shank diameter and width less than 1/16 of the shank diameter, with no intersecting cracks.
- Where a rivet was removed, the vacated hole is round at nominal size with no elongation, tearout or crack, and the skin shows no drill or punch gouging.
- A written record identifies the damage type and class, states why patching rather than replacement was chosen, and records the material and rivet selections used.

sources.condition: Rectangular cutout corner radius no smaller than 1/2 inch
sources.note: Verbatim: "make the radius of curvature at each corner no smaller than 1⁄2-inch".

sources.condition: 3/32-inch stop holes at crack ends
sources.note: Verbatim: "Stop holes—drill 3/32" diameter holes in each sharp corner"; figure text is machine-extracted, PDF is authority.

sources.condition: Filler same gauge/material as skin; doubler one gauge heavier
sources.note: Verbatim: "The filler must be of the same gauge and material as the original skin. The doubler should be of material one gauge heavier than the skin."

sources.condition: Rivet diameter = next larger size above 3 x skin thickness
sources.note: Verbatim: "multiply the thickness of the skin by three and use the next larger size rivet corresponding to that figure".

sources.condition: Minimum edge distance 1/4" for 1/8" rivets, 5/16" for 5/32"
sources.note: Verbatim: "Minimum edge distance using 1/8" rivets is 1/4" and using 5/32" rivets is 5/16"." Stated for lap patch.

sources.condition: Rivet head crack limits (depth <1/8 D, width <1/16 D, no intersecting)
sources.note: Verbatim: depth "less than 1⁄8 of the shank diameter", width "less than 1⁄16 of the shank diameter".

sources.condition: Shop head approx. 0.5D height, 1.5D width
sources.source: AM.II.A.S6 procedure sheet, Rivet the Material, Senior Mechanic Note 5
sources.note: Campus figure: "preferred height = 0.5D, preferred width = 1.5D". Not found in the handbook pages supplied.

sources.condition: Finished hole at least 0.003" over rivet diameter; #40 pilot
sources.source: AM.II.A.S6 procedure sheet, Drill the Holes, Senior Mechanic Notes 6 and 17
sources.note: Campus figures, including #30 (0.1285") for a -4 rivet. Not in the handbook extract given.

sources.condition: Damage classification and repair-vs-replace decision recorded
sources.note: Handbook directs "Determine if repair would be the best procedure" and defines damage repairable by patching.

sources.condition: Deburr all holes both faces; edges smoothed
sources.source: AM.II.A.S6 procedure sheet, Drill the Holes step 7; handbook p. 4-92 "Smooth out any abrasions and/or dents"
sources.note: Handbook damage-removal list supports smoothing; the both-faces hole deburr requirement is the campus sheet's.

not_photo_gradeable: Shop head height and width against the 0.5D/1.5D targets — requires a rivet gauge or caliper reading, not a still.
Finished hole diameter being at least 0.003 inch over rivet diameter — needs pin gauge or caliper.
Gauge and alloy of doubler and filler stock (same gauge as skin / one gauge heavier) — needs a micrometer reading or stock certification.
Whether the filler is truly flush rather than within a few thousandths of a step — light and shadow suggest it but do not measure it.
Deburring of the faying (hidden) faces of every hole, since those surfaces are enclosed once the stack is assembled.
Drill and punch perpendicularity, single light punch blow, backing of thin parts, and equalised gun/bucking-bar pressure — process conditions visible only in video.
Progression from coarse to fine grit during edge smoothing.
Rivet gun regulator set to a controllable recoil, and set tightened to a felt torque rise.
Whether cracks were stop-drilled before cutting or after, and whether NDI was used where a visual check is inconclusive.
